# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤏 🤞 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 🤏 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤙 🖐 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤙 🤏 🖐]

The bomb currently shows display `3`, green light, and three wires in order: blue, yellow, green. I am telling both teammates so the Mute can match this state to the manual and the Blind can inspect the physical controls accordingly. The gesture sequences from the Mute have no established meaning for me yet.

```text
speak(text="Bomb state: display 3. Indicator light green. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, use the manual to determine the required action and communicate it through your gesture code. Blind, report the tactile controls and wait for the instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤟]

I still cannot infer a meaning from the Mute’s gestures because no gesture code has been established. The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I will ask the Mute to define a fixed encoding and ask the Blind for the tactile controls; no physical action should be taken yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received [🤏 🤟] but do not know its meaning. Establish a code in plain words: send one gesture for each wire number, and use a fixed gesture to mean cut or press. Then resend the instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state remains display 3, green light, wires blue yellow green. I am waiting for the Mute to clarify the manual instruction. Report every tactile control and do not activate anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👊]

The visible bomb state is unchanged. The Mute’s latest signs are still not self-interpreting: first an index-up hand, V sign, “I love you” sign, and fist; then “I love you” sign and fist. I will relay their exact order to the Blind and require an explicit, shared code before any control is operated.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state remains display 3, green light, wires blue yellow green. The Mute just gestured: index-up, V sign, I-love-you sign, fist; then I-love-you sign, fist. These are not yet assigned meanings. Do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your latest gestures as index-up, V sign, I-love-you sign, fist; then I-love-you sign, fist. Please state the intended wire and operation plainly to the Blind, and establish what each gesture means before we act.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👊]

The bomb’s visible state remains unchanged. The repeated `[🤟 👊]` is not inherently meaningful, so I am establishing a shared code now: the first gesture identifies the wire (`☝` = 1, `✌` = 2, `🤟` = 3), and the second identifies the operation (`👊` = cut). Under this code, the latest message would mean “cut wire 3,” but the Mute must confirm that this is the intended encoding before the Blind acts.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="We need a fixed code. Use first gesture for wire: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Use second gesture for operation: 👊 means cut. Your latest [🤟 👊] would therefore mean cut wire 3. Confirm by repeating [🤟 👊] if that is correct; otherwise send the correct two gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute's latest signal was [🤟 👊]. I am defining a code where that means cut wire 3, but this is not confirmed yet. Do not cut anything until I confirm.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👊]

The Mute has repeated `[🤟 👊]` after I proposed that code, which serves as confirmation: wire 3, then cut. The visible wire colors remain blue, yellow, green, so wire 3 is the green wire. I am instructing the Blind to cut only wire 3.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: cut wire 3, the green wire. Do not touch or cut wires 1 or 2.")
wait()
```
